newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian dropout claims he can make fuel from herb.
newsitem.headline: Indian dropout claims he can make fuel from herb.

text.p: A south Indian state offered financial backing on Monday to a high school dropout who claims he can make fuel from a green herb and a secret chemical.
Ramar Pillai demonstrated how he makes his purported herbal fuel to M. Karunanidhi, chief minister of Tamil Nadu state, and reporters in the state capital Madras.
"It doesn't seem to me to be a conjurer's trick or plain magic," Karunanidhi said after the demonstration.
"Having seen it with my own eyes, it is indeed petrol... If it is proved to be a viable proposition, poverty might vanish from Tamil Nadu."
The 36-year-old amateur scientist said he first noticed that the herb, when burned, emitted a smell of petrol while on a 1973 camping trip in the jungle.

"We have a long way to go before the process is accepted scientifically and its commercial credentials are established," said V. Murugesan, a professor in the department of chemical engineering in Anna University in Madras.
